newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN LABOUR INFLEXIBILITY SEEN OVERESTIMATED.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN LABOUR INFLEXIBILITY SEEN OVERESTIMATED.

text.p: South Africa's labour market had areas of inflexibility that needed to be addressed, although the existing degree of rigidity was generally overestimated, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Thursday.

Addressing a Chemical Workers Industrial Union conference, Mboweni said government's approach to the labour market, which the International Labour Organisation (ILO) has described as too flexible in some respects, was one of "regulated flexibility".
"Our approach is that where there are unnecessary rigidities in our labour market and our economy they must be removed," Mboweni said.

"But this should not be done in ways which undermine labour security and union rights in particular," he said. "Indeed, as the ILO suggests, in some areas there is a need for more regulation," he said.
Mboweni said areas where labour market inflexibility and labour security needed to be enhanced included:
* an excessive focus on procedural aspects rather than fairness when considering dismissal for misconduct;
* a labour law which gave inadequate protection to farm workers;
* certain wage setting mechanisms which did not take adequate account of differing realities in certain regions, sectors and small or new business;
